title: Zoom in: the life of one idempotency key
caption: A key is claimed, worked under a lease, finished with its stored response, replayed on every retry, and finally expired.

steps.text: The request arrives with key 7f3a. Look it up in the key table.
No row: insert it as in_progress with the request hash and a 30 s lease. The unique index makes this the only winner.
Charge the card and send the key along, so the processor dedups as well.
The processor answers: approved (or declined; a decline is an outcome too).
Save the full response with the key and mark it done, in the same transaction as the payment row.
Any later retry finds the row done and gets the stored response byte for byte, until the key expires after 7 days.

scenarios.name: Crash mid-charge
scenarios.summary: The worker dies after calling the processor: the lease lets a retry take over, and the processor's own dedup prevents a second charge.

steps.text: Attempt 1 claims the key and calls the processor.
Its pod is killed before it stores anything. The row stays in_progress.
The client retries. The row is found, still in_progress.
The 30 s lease has run out, so this attempt takes over the key.
It charges again with the same key; the processor returns the first charge instead of making a new one. Store and reply.

scenarios.name: Outcome unknown
scenarios.summary: The processor times out: the money may or may not have moved. Don't guess; keep the key pending until the truth arrives.

steps.text: The processor call times out after 10 s.
Marking it failed would invite a retry with a fresh key (double charge); marking it done would be a lie. Leave it pending and tell the app 'processing'.
The webhook or a status query by key settles it later; only then is the response stored and the key done.

scenarios.name: Concurrent retry
scenarios.summary: A double-tap sends two requests 50 ms apart: the second must not wait forever, and must not start a second charge.

steps.text: Request A claims the key and starts charging.
Request B arrives with the same key and finds in_progress.
A's lease is still valid, so B gets 409 with Retry-After: 1 instead of holding a connection.
B retries a second later, finds done, and gets A's response.
